stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category. For every $U\in\Ob(\mathcal C)$ write $h_U(T)=\Mor_{\mathcal C}(T,U)$, a contravariant functor into sets, and let $h:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C)$ send $U$ to $h_U$ and a morphism to postcomposition.
Let $U, V \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Given any morphism of functors $s : h_U \to h_V$
there is a unique morphism $\phi : U \to V$
such that $h(\phi) = s$. In other words the
functor $h$ is fully faithful. More generally,
given any contravariant functor $F$ and any object
$U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we have a natural bijection
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(h_U, F) \longrightarrow F(U),
\quad
s \longmapsto s_U(\text{id}_U).
$$
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category. For each $U$ define $h_U=\Mor_{\mathcal C}(-,U)$, with Yoneda map $h:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C)$.
conclusions: For every $U,V\in\Ob(\mathcal C)$ and every natural transformation $s:h_U\to h_V$, there is a unique $\phi:U\to V$ such that $h(\phi)=s$, so $h$ is fully faithful.

For every contravariant set-valued functor $F$ on $\mathcal C$ and every $U\in\Ob(\mathcal C)$, evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_U$ gives a natural bijection $\Mor_{\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C)}(h_U,F)\cong F(U)$.

reason: Evaluates a natural transformation at the identity for the representable case; constructs inverse natural transformation from element of F(U).
